chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the junub and the menstruating woman taking from the mosque an item that may be in it.
He said: “Yes, but they should not place anything in the mosque.”

Then he said—may Allah, Exalted is He, support him: Nor should he touch a name from among the Names of Allah, Exalted is He, written on a tablet, a sheet, a stone setting, or other than that. This indicates that.

key_terms.أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ: the Names of Allah written in visible form
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْمَتَاعَ: an item or belonging kept in the mosque
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque as a sacred space with legal rulings
key_terms.فَصٍّ: a stone setting or engraved gem
key_terms.لَوْحٍ: a tablet or board on which something is written

ai.seo_question: Can a junub or a menstruating woman take something from a mosque or touch the written Name of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a junub and a menstruating woman in relation to the mosque. It permits taking an item from the mosque while prohibiting placing something into it, and it also indicates the prohibition of touching the written Name of Allah in a state of ritual impurity.
